entry_state: The finite debt model separates price, promised repayment, default loss, issue fees, policy incentives and shareholder participation. Positive surplus alone does not guarantee credible repayment or funding. Conversion then introduces an independent question about control, accounting dates and the intervening control history, which vote percentages or endpoint assessments do not resolve.
exit_state: Acquisition reporting requires a supported control date, business scope, measured assets/liabilities/consideration and separate prior-interest and NCI choices. Post-control profit, OCI, cash and revisions retain their own dates and bases. The conditional symbolic worksheet preserves these requirements without inventing measurements or actual authority admission.

observations.finding: Separate-investment reporting, consolidation, business-combination scope and substantive control are distinguished. The optional concentration test is not treated as a positive business test. Historical editions, later amendments and missing entity facts remain explicit; balanced journals and economic prices do not fill measurement slots.
observations.disposition: retain the stated source-scope distinctions; no new external standards verification is claimed by this rendered read

observations.finding: The existing full-ownership stable-perimeter method requires whole-interval control and explicit calendar/measurement compatibility. Endpoint ownership or a source-history hash does not authorize a mid-period acquisition or provide the missing accounting method.
observations.disposition: retain the distinction between a valid scope refusal and an implementation failure on an admitted unchanged-period fixture
